name: CA-01
label: Likely D

key_factors: Post-redistricting lean of D+7 favors Democrats
Gallagher is an incumbent who has already won this seat, tempering the lean
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%
No public general-election polling in the race
model.rationale: The district's D+7 lean and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win around 95% point clearly toward McGuire, but Gallagher's incumbency and his demonstrated ability to win here justify pulling the expected margin well below the fundamentals-only estimate. With no polls available, uncertainty stays elevated.
model.watch: Any credible general-election poll showing Gallagher within single digits, or a shift in national House conditions toward Republicans, would move this toward a tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern California's first district became considerably more Democratic after redistricting, with a partisan lean of about seven points toward Democrats, yet Republican incumbent James Gallagher holds the seat and is running for reelection. State Senator Mike McGuire, a well-known Democratic figure in the region, challenges him and has slightly out-raised the incumbent, with modest outside support on the Democratic side.

Prediction markets strongly favor a Democratic pickup, and the district's fundamentals point the same direction. Still, Gallagher's incumbency and prior win here argue against treating the race as safe for either side, so the forecast lands as likely Democratic with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
